title: command pallet - dock - does not load correctly

judgment.rationale: The initial report describes an invisible dock that still reserves display space, while replies say reinstalling restored a visible default dock and lost prior layout settings. The attached report contains unresolved pinned-command warnings but does not identify whether DockSettings were lost, provider IDs failed to resolve, or the dock failed to render. Ask for the post-reinstall state and preserved settings, not another generic log upload.
evidence: The initial report describes PowerToys 0.102.2933 after reboot: dock invisible although windows are displaced; restart and Dock/Command Palette toggles did not fix it.

The attached 0.102.2933 CmdPal log has repeated DockViewModel.SetupBands warnings that pinned provider/command IDs could not be found; these establish unresolved bands, not the cause of the invisible window or settings loss.

The first reply says reinstall restored Command Palette but left Dock disabled; re-enabling showed defaults and prior Dock settings were missing. A second commenter reports the dock returned with defaults after reinstall.

At upstream main 9227a8497750, DockSettings stores global/per-monitor bands by provider/command IDs; SetupBands warns and skips unresolved commands. This makes settings and command resolution relevant but does not establish which failed: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/Dock/DockViewModel.cs#L239-L259
judgment.recommended_action: Confirm whether the issue persists and preserve relevant Dock settings before any further reset

fix_assessment.rationale: The replies show a visible default dock after reinstall, not whether the original invisible dock was caused by configuration loss or rendering/provider resolution. Keep the fix direction conditional.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve or reconcile Dock settings across the confirmed update path
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis only: an update/reinstall path may fail to restore saved Dock settings or resolve pinned provider/command IDs; the warnings and default-layout reports do not select between these causes.
plan: Compare only relevant DockSettings fields before/after update if prior configuration is available, preserving any backup before further changes.
If settings remain present, trace the unresolved IDs through SetupBands; if settings disappeared, trace persistence/migration instead of adding a provider workaround.
Track dock-window visibility and saved band layout as separate outcomes.
verification: After the same update/restart sequence, the dock is visible and pre-existing enabled state, band layout, and per-monitor choices remain intact; unavailable bands are identified rather than silently replaced by defaults.

confidence.rationale: The logs and replies show missing band resolution/default settings but do not establish which persistence or rendering branch caused the original symptom.

issue_context.summary: The dock was invisible while reserving display space, then returned with defaults after reinstall according to the reporter and a second user.
known_information: The initial report identifies PowerToys 0.102.2933 and includes a diagnostic report ZIP captured before reinstall.
That report's CmdPal log contains repeated SetupBands warnings for pinned commands that could not be found.
The reporter says reinstall restored Command Palette, left Dock disabled, and re-enabling displayed defaults; another commenter also says reinstall restored a default dock.
The issue does not provide pre/post DockSettings data or confirm whether the dock still fails after defaults were restored.
inferences: Unresolved pinned commands may explain missing dock contents, but cannot alone explain the invisible reserved window or prove settings were deleted.
The default layout may reflect reset/migration or a new settings profile; the evidence does not distinguish these.
issue_context.analysis: The attached report was reviewed rather than requesting duplicate generic logs. Its unresolved-band warnings and the source's provider/command-ID settings model make the exact post-install state discriminating evidence. Preserve the invisible window and lost layout as separate observations.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete body and both comments plus PowerToysReport_2026-10-22-10-19-22.zip. CmdPal log has SetupBands unresolved-ID warnings but no post-reinstall settings snapshot.

Inspected DockViewModel.SetupBands and DockSettings at upstream main 9227a8497750: unresolved commands are skipped; global and per-monitor bands are serialized by provider/command IDs: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/9227a8497750c257a0682b53c556d07f48ed8ff3/src/modules/cmdpal/Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.ViewModels/Settings/DockSettings.cs#L20-L116
Focused CmdPal Dock/settings issue search and local source history surfaced no exact duplicate or source change establishing coverage of this upgrade/reinstall report.

information_gaps.information: Whether the invisible-dock problem remains after reinstall and whether the customized layout was absent from saved settings or present but not rendered/resolved.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates rendering/command-resolution failure from settings migration/loss and determines whether the original bug still reproduces.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Confirm the current Dock state. If available, compare only Dock enabled/band/provider/command fields before and after reinstall, redacting account-specific paths and unrelated pins; if invisibility recurs before reset, comment /bugreport first and preserve settings.

actions.label: Confirm current Dock state and saved layout

comment.body: Thanks for confirming that reinstalling brought back a visible Dock with default settings, and for the second report of the same default-layout result. I reviewed the attached 0.102.2933 report: its CmdPal log already contains warnings that saved dock band commands could not be resolved, so another generic log upload is not needed. Could you confirm whether the Dock still fails now, and whether the old custom layout was absent from saved Dock settings or present but not rendered? If available, share only relevant enabled/band/provider/command fields with account-specific paths and unrelated pins redacted. If invisibility recurs before reinstall/reset, comment /bugreport first and preserve the settings.
